outcome: Rupture of membranes longer than 24 hours
cohort: The study included 964 primiparous women (482 with normal BMI and 482 with obese BMI) enrolled for care at freestanding birth centers in the United States, identified from the American Association of Birth Centers Perinatal Data Registry.
finding: The majority of women with obese BMIs experienced uncomplicated perinatal courses and vaginal births, with no significant differences found in antenatal complications, prolonged pregnancy/labor, prolonged rupture of membranes, postpartum hemorrhage, or newborn outcomes when compared to women with normal BMIs.
mod_finding: Primiparous women with obesity who started labor at a birth center had a 30.7% transfer rate and an 11.1% cesarean birth rate.
